name: Runner Extras - Precompiled Implicit Return
brief: Issue #3710: calling Microsoft's PRECOMPILED AL must yield the value BC's own AL specifies -- true for a [TryFunction] whose body completed, false for a plain Boolean method whose body fell off the end. Codeunit 2000 'Time Series Management'.GetMLForecastCredentials is a [TryFunction] and correctly answers true; Codeunit 7046 'Price Asset - G/L Account'.ValidateUnitOfMeasure is a plain method and correctly answers false.
description: The BC claim these rest on -- what a [TryFunction] with no exit returns, and how it differs from a plain method with no exit -- is plain BC behaviour and is pinned upstream by corpus codeunit 60349 'Test CU TryFunc NoExit Return' against a real service tier. What stays here is the runner-specific half: that calling MICROSOFT'S PRECOMPILED copies of both shapes yields those same two answers. A corpus test cannot express that, because naming a precompiled method requires calling one. Keeping both precompiled arms is what makes the suite discriminate -- a runner answering true for every precompiled method, or false for every one, fails exactly one of them. #3710 originally recorded Codeunit 2000's true as a defect, reading its SymbolReference ReturnTypeDefinition Boolean without the adjacent Attributes entry naming TryFunction; the Boolean is the attribute's synthesized return, and the runner was correct.
